key_insight: SCCL-DT reduces false-negative supervision in chest X-ray contrastive learning by using adaptive, semantic-conflict-aware masking plus dual-rule teacher distillation for zero-shot diagnosis.
clinical_relevance: This could improve zero-shot chest X-ray triage support by making vision-language models better at recognizing shared findings across patients instead of over-penalizing similar cases.
method: Tracks image-report similarity with EMA statistics to set adaptive thresholds.
Hard-masks likely semantic conflicts before softmax, instead of treating all off-diagonal pairs as negatives.
Uses two teachers with OR and AND rules, then distills them into one student model.
evidence_signal: On five public chest X-ray benchmarks, the model reports a mean zero-shot AUC of 0.850 versus 0.837 for the strongest compared baseline.
watch_item: The abstract notes that the online-mask audit only suggests finding agreement and does not prove clinical equivalence, so thresholding and masking may still be sensitive to dataset shift.
paper_title: SCCL-DT: Semantic-Conflict-Aware Contrastive Learning with Dual-Rule Teacher Distillation for Zero-Shot Chest X-Ray Diagnosis
